messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER — Serving runtime errors detected in us-west-2 cluster (severity: high). Alert: 502/504 spike + container restarts on serving pool 'gpt-xl-pool'. First observed at 2026-05-11T02:44:36Z. Pager: @emma :rotating_light:
emma: I'm on it, paging into thread. seeing ~30% error rate on /v1/generate and a bunch of 'CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION' and 'kernel timeout' lines in pod logs. Also multiple kubelet logs with 'Network I/O timeout' followed by container restart.
raj: adding context — infra metrics show increased packet retransmits on IB fabric between racks r12 and r13 starting ~02:40Z. Latency on RDMA endpoints spiked to 100-200ms for short bursts.
sasha: customer-impact: CS reported degraded latency for two midsize customers (app-echo and searchlytics). Both hit retries and saw 5xxs. I'm starting an incident page for customer comms.
ops-jen: copying logs from one affected pod: ```
2026-05-11T02:43:12Z serving: error - ping: timeout
2026-05-11T02:43:12Z runtime: KV cache miss
2026-05-11T02:43:13Z cuda: kernel launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
2026-05-11T02:43:20Z kubelet: container restarted (OOM suspected)
2026-05-11T02:43:21Z rdma: cm event: path_migrate
2026-05-11T02:43:21Z rdma: retry counter incremented
```
emma: thanks. I'm shifting traffic off gpt-xl-pool to gpt-xl-fallback to reduce customer impact and to give us a stable baseline. Rolling routing change now (canary -> 20% fallback).
infra-bot: route-change: traffic % to gpt-xl-fallback = 20% (applied).
raj: runbook step 1: validate IB ports and counters. Commands: `ibstat -p`, `ibv_devinfo -v`, `ethtool -S <iface>`, check mlx5_core err counters. Can someone run on node r12-n05 and r13-n02?
ops-jen: on r12-n05: `ibv_devinfo` shows link up but port counters: `port_rcv_errors` spiked, `port_xmit_discards` increased. ethtool: `tx_err` and `rx_err` higher than normal. dmesg has repeated `mlx5_core: PF VF parity` messages and `DR RQ timeout`.
sasha: that aligns with packet reorders/timeouts — fabric causing RDMA connections to stall which surfaces to the serving runtime as long-tail RPCs -> KV cache staleness -> GPU kernel timeouts -> container restarts.
emma: mitigation plan: 1) move serving pool off affected hosts, 2) temporarily disable RDMA transport for serving runtime on new nodes (force TCP over libfabric), 3) if nodes continue to misbehave, cordon + drain and reboot NICs. Who can disable RDMA transport on the next rollout?
raj: I can push a quick config flip to runtime: set ENV INF_TRANSPORT=tcp for the canary group. This will avoid RDMA and should remove kernel-level stalls at cost of some latency. Preparing patch now.
ops-jen: note — disabling RDMA requires restarting the runtime process; plan for rolling restarts with minimal capacity reduction.
infra-bot: change-request created: infra/rdma-firewall-checks #563.
ops-jen: quick health check after initial 20% shift and INF_TRANSPORT flip on canary: errors drop to ~8% on canary, overall cluster error rate down to ~18% (from 30%). Latency increased +45ms p50 on canary, p95 stable.
sasha: good. escalate communications: CS bulletin draft to affected customers: `We observed brief networking instability affecting inference latency and errors; we've moved traffic to fallback and temporarily disabled RDMA on canary hosts; investigating hardware fabric with vendor.` I'll publish if we hold.
emma: proceeding to flip INF_TRANSPORT for the rest of gpt-xl-pool in 2 waves. We'll keep 10% traffic on RDMA for observation.
raj: executing config rollout. Command used: ```
kubectl set env ds/rt-serving INF_TRANSPORT=tcp -n production --selector=pool=gpt-xl-canary
# then restart ds pods one by one with gracefulDrain
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l pool=gpt-xl-canary -o name); do kubectl rollout restart $pod -n production; sleep 15; done
```
ops-jen: during restarts we saw one node (r13-n02) with kubelet reporting `failed to sync network status` and extra container restarts. I'm cordoning r13-n02 now.
ops-jen: `kubectl cordon r13-n02` -> `node/r13-n02 cordoned` — moving pods off.
raj: while evacuating, observed that one serving container crashed with OOM but logs show slow RDMA reads earlier -> memory growth due to repeated retries and larger KV caches filling up. We'll also reduce max_cache_entries to 40k to limit memory pressure. Applying env: `MAX_KV_CACHE=40000`.
sasha: customer-success-bot: Customer impact update prepared: customers (app-echo, searchlytics, two dev orgs) — degraded but recovering. Recommend proactive notice: 'We mitigated by routing and switching to TCP transport; some requests may see transient latency increases.'
emma: infra team please engage NIC vendor TAC — share mlx5 core logs and counters. Raj, can you collect `mlx5_core` and `dmesg` bundles from affected hosts and upload to the incident workspace?
raj: collected and uploaded to /incidents/1842109876/artifacts: `r12-n05_dmesg.txt`, `r13-n02_dmesg.txt`, `ib_counters_r12-r13.csv`. Also ran `ibv_rc_pingpong` between nodes and saw ~30% packet loss during bursts.
ops-jen: after full INF_TRANSPORT=tcp rollout for pool, cluster error rate down to 3% — stable for 10m. No new CUDA kernel errors reported in restarted pods.
emma: next steps: 1) keep RDMA disabled for serving pools until vendor TAC confirms fix OR until we can schedule NIC firmware upgrade in a maintenance window; 2) bring evacuated nodes back after NIC/firmware validation; 3) postmortem to include trigger, detection timelines, mitigation steps, and a checklist for RDMA->TCP flip.
infra-bot: maintenance-ticket created: NIC-FW-UPGRADE #789 scheduled tentative 2026-05-11T23:00Z (needs coord).
ops-jen: one follow-up — we should add a runtime guard that autoswitches transport to tcp after X RDMA retried events to auto-degrade instead of manual flip. Filing runtime enhancement: RT-1974.
sasha: incident severity -> Sev2 (customer impact limited, workaround in place). I’ll initiate SEV2 postmortem and draft timeline.
emma: hands off to oncall rotation — @raj you remain primary for infra, @ops-jen for runtime changes; I'll join postmortem. Switching channel to #incident-postmortems once stabilized. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged. Severity: 2. Pager duty: cleared 2026-05-11T03:12:56Z.
